modules.name: uart_tx
modules.description: Serialize accepted bytes as fixed-rate 115200 bit/s 8N1 frames.

parameters.name: C_CLKS_PER_BIT
parameters.description: 100 MHz clocks in one UART bit

ports.name: i_data
ports.description: Byte offered by the packet encoder

ports.name: o_busy
ports.description: A complete character is being sent

behavior: A byte is accepted only on a rising edge where i_data_valid and o_data_ready are both high.
The accepted byte is sent as one low start bit, eight LSB-first data bits, and one high stop bit; every bit lasts exactly C_CLKS_PER_BIT clocks.
o_data_ready remains low and o_busy remains high for the entire ten-bit frame; the byte input is ignored while busy.
After reset the serial line is high, the transmitter is idle, and the input interface is ready.
constraints: No derived or gated clock is permitted.
C_CLKS_PER_BIT is fixed to 868 in the Basys 3 integration.
The upstream valid-ready source must keep i_data stable until acceptance.
corner_cases: Bytes 0x00 and 0xFF preserve all identical data bits.
An input valid assertion while busy is not accepted and cannot replace the active frame.
A new byte may be accepted on the first rising edge after the previous stop bit completes.
verification_cases: TX_RESET_IDLE: reset leaves o_uart_tx high, o_busy low, and o_data_ready high.
TX_BYTE_PATTERNS: 0x00, 0xFF, 0xA5, and 0x3C match the complete 8N1 wire order.
TX_BIT_LENGTH: every start, data, and stop bit lasts exactly 868 clocks.
TX_BACKPRESSURE: o_data_ready stays low throughout an active frame.

timing_diagrams.title: Accepted byte serialization
timing_diagrams.description: One accepted byte drives a start bit, eight LSB-first data intervals, and a stop bit before ready returns.

modules.name: uart_rx
modules.description: Synchronize and sample a fixed-rate 115200 bit/s 8N1 input into a held valid-ready byte output.

parameters.name: C_CLKS_PER_BIT
parameters.description: 100 MHz clocks in one UART bit

parameters.name: C_HALF_BIT_CLKS
parameters.description: Clocks from start detection to start-bit confirmation

ports.name: o_data_valid
ports.description: Received byte is available and stable

ports.name: o_frame_error
ports.description: One-clock pulse for a low sampled stop bit

ports.name: o_busy
ports.description: Receiver is sampling an active character

behavior: i_uart_rx passes through two serially connected sampling registers before start detection.
A low candidate start is confirmed after C_HALF_BIT_CLKS clocks; a returned high level is rejected as a false start.
Eight data bits and the stop bit are sampled C_CLKS_PER_BIT clocks apart at their nominal centers.
A valid byte remains stable with o_data_valid high until i_data_ready is high on a rising edge.
A low stop sample suppresses o_data_valid and raises o_frame_error for one system clock.
constraints: No derived or gated clock is permitted.
The asynchronous serial input must remain connected only through the two-register synchronizer.
The one-entry output buffer intentionally stops detecting new starts while backpressured.
corner_cases: A low pulse shorter than half a bit is rejected without producing a byte.
The output byte and valid flag remain unchanged during downstream backpressure.
Transmit bit periods from 851 through 885 system clocks cover the directed minus/plus two percent mismatch cases.
A low stop bit produces exactly one frame-error pulse and no valid byte.
verification_cases: RX_NOMINAL: 0xA5 is reconstructed from an 868-clock 8N1 frame.
RX_CLOCK_MISMATCH: 0x96 and 0x69 are recovered at 851-clock and 885-clock transmitter bit periods.
RX_BACKPRESSURE: 0x3C remains stable for at least twenty clocks while i_data_ready is low.
RX_BAD_STOP: a low stop bit raises one error pulse and does not submit a byte.
RX_FALSE_START: a 100-clock low pulse returns to idle without a byte.

timing_diagrams.title: Centered 8N1 receive sampling
timing_diagrams.description: The synchronized start is confirmed at half a bit, then data and stop levels are sampled one full bit apart before valid is held.
